subject.title: [Feature Request] ACP Session Skill Context Injection

question: Should OpenClaw add a core ACP skill-context injection contract for `sessions_spawn`, and which selection modes plus redaction, observability, prompt-layer, and resume semantics are allowed?
rationale: The source gap is clear, but the feature changes a core session/security boundary and interacts with Codex-native skill behavior, so automation should not choose the permanent contract.

options.title: Design core ACP contract first
options.body: Keep the issue open while maintainers specify allowed selection modes, redaction/audit metadata, prompt layer, and Codex/native parity requirements before implementation.

options.title: Limit to explicit skill IDs
options.body: Scope a narrower API around `sessions_spawn` explicit skill IDs only, deferring auto/default selection until observability and privacy behavior are proven.

options.title: Decline ACP injection
options.body: Keep ACP harnesses isolated from OpenClaw-rendered skill content and point users to harness-native skills or MCP/plugin workflows instead.

recommendation.title: Design core ACP contract first
recommendation.body: Keep the issue open while maintainers specify allowed selection modes, redaction/audit metadata, prompt layer, and Codex/native parity requirements before implementation.

likelyOwner.reason: They have the strongest current history signal on the ACP sessions and runtime contract that this decision would change.
